chunks.content: 96 The Hidden Cost of Higher Valuations Hi Sara, Private equity is flooding into the accounting firm space. Valuations are rising. Buyers are circling. On the surface, it looks like a seller’s dream. But here’s what no one’s talking about: Higher valuations are quietly killing the traditional family succession plan. Last year alone, I saw five owners pass over their own children - children who had been working in the business for years - because third-party buyers could offer more. Why? Because: Valuations have jumped Interest rates make internal buyouts unaffordable SBA loans are normalizing 90% cash at close-hard to compete with that When you can sell for several million dollars tomorrow, most sellers aren’t going to accept a 10-year buyout from their child at a fraction of the price. And most parents don’t want their kid saddled with that kind of debt. It’s not a moral failing. It’s math. That math has real consequences, especially for buyers stepping into family-run firms. If the seller’s child is still working in the business, you’re walking into a complex emotional and legal situation. And without a solid employment agreement, that person could leave and take clients with them. This shift isn’t just about who’s buying. It’s about how succession works now. Curious how to navigate succession when emotions (and millions of dollars) are on the line? Watch the full breakdown here. Because making a smart exit shouldn't mean torching the family tree.
